clauses.scope: These policies apply only to fictional full-time employees of {company}. All entitlements and workflows are demonstration rules. They do not describe a real employer or establish legal employment rights.
clauses.schedule: The standard schedule is {work_days}, {start_hour:02d}:00 to {end_hour:02d}:00 in {timezone}, with a {break_minutes}-minute unpaid break. This yields {daily_hours} paid working hours per day and {weekly_hours} per full workweek. A business day is a scheduled workday excluding company-declared holidays; calendar days include weekends and holidays.
clauses.core_hours: On working days, employees are available during core hours from {core_start_hour:02d}:00 to {core_end_hour:02d}:00 in {timezone}, except for their unpaid break, approved leave or a documented accommodation. Managers may approve a shifted schedule that preserves paid hours; core hours still apply unless People Operations records an exception.
clauses.approvals: The manager reviews routine requests within {approval_business_days} business days. Silence is not approval. If the manager is unavailable, People Operations assigns an alternate approver. Exceptions require a written People Operations decision with its scope and end date; an exception does not silently replace the published policy.
clauses.annual_entitlement: Annual leave is {annual_leave_days} paid working days per calendar year for a full-year employee. Joiners receive a prorated allocation based on calendar days employed in that year, rounded up to the next {leave_unit_days}-day unit. People Operations records the allocation in the fictional leave register at onboarding. The allocation is separate from sick leave and company-declared holidays.
clauses.annual_request: Annual leave is requested at least {annual_notice_business_days} business days before its start and requires manager approval before absence. Urgent requests may use the documented exception process. Annual leave can be used from the start date; there is no onboarding waiting period. A full leave day deducts one scheduled working day and a half day deducts {leave_unit_days} day. Holidays and non-working days are not deducted.
clauses.annual_carryover: Up to {carryover_days} unused annual leave days carry into the next calendar year and must be used by the end of March. Older carried leave is consumed before the new allocation. Annual leave above the carryover limit expires at year end under these fictional rules; People Operations records any approved exception. Sick leave never converts into annual leave.
clauses.sick_leave: Sick leave is a separate allocation of {sick_leave_days} paid working days per calendar year; joiners use the same calendar-day proration and {leave_unit_days}-day rounding rule as annual leave. Notify the manager and People Operations before the scheduled start when practicable, or as soon as reasonably possible during an emergency. Prior approval is not required for an unexpected illness. People Operations records the absence after notification; diagnoses and medical documents are never entered into this demo dataset.
clauses.sick_balance: Sick leave is taken in {leave_unit_days}-day units, does not carry over and is not paid out. If sick leave is exhausted, an employee may request available annual leave or an unpaid absence; neither conversion happens automatically. Approved sick leave is an excused absence for attendance purposes.
clauses.onboarding: Before the start date, People Operations opens a fictional onboarding checklist and records the role, manager role, start date and work arrangement. IT prepares a managed device and access limited to the role after manager approval. No real employee identity, contact details, credentials or confidential documents belong in this demonstration checklist.
clauses.onboarding_schedule: On the start date, the manager explains the schedule, leave process, security responsibilities and role expectations. Mandatory orientation and security training occur during paid hours within the first {onboarding_business_days} business days. People Operations verifies completion, and the manager holds an onboarding review after {onboarding_review_calendar_days} calendar days. Missing training is escalated for scheduling rather than extending work hours automatically.
clauses.remote_work: Eligible roles may request up to {remote_days_per_week} remote working days per workweek. The manager must approve the arrangement and record agreed remote days, coverage and a review date in the fictional work-arrangement register. Remote work can begin during onboarding when access, device and training requirements are met. Approval depends on role suitability and coverage, not on a separate leave allowance.
clauses.remote_safety: Remote days follow the same schedule, paid hours, core availability and attendance rules as office days. Use a managed device, approved connection methods and a workspace that protects business information. Report loss of connectivity to the manager when possible; the manager arranges alternative work or a documented absence. Remote work does not count as leave, and approved leave removes the expectation of availability. International remote arrangements require a separate People Operations review and are outside this demo policy.
clauses.attendance: Record actual start, finish and break periods in the fictional attendance register by the next business day. Correct errors through the manager rather than recording time that was not worked. Notify the manager as soon as possible about lateness or an unplanned absence. Approved leave, company-declared holidays and documented accommodations are excused; they are not treated as unapproved absence.
clauses.extra_hours: Work beyond the standard paid schedule requires prior manager approval and a recorded People Operations arrangement for compensating time. This dataset does not define a statutory overtime rate. Employees must not work unrecorded extra hours to make up approved leave or routine remote days.
clauses.offboarding_notice: For a routine voluntary departure, provide {offboarding_notice_calendar_days} calendar days of notice to the manager and People Operations. They confirm the final working date and handover plan; a shorter notice period needs a written People Operations exception. Involuntary or urgent security departures use a separately reviewed process and are not simulated as routine voluntary departures here.
clauses.offboarding_leave: The ordinary schedule and leave rules continue through the final working date. Approved annual or sick leave may occur during notice; it does not automatically extend that date. People Operations recalculates the annual allocation through the final date using the original proration rule, then pays any positive unused earned annual balance in the final settlement. Sick leave is not paid out. Any negative balance or payroll dispute requires manual People Operations review; this policy authorizes no automatic deduction.
clauses.offboarding_access: The manager signs off the handover before the final working day ends. IT revokes access at the end of that working day, or earlier only under an explicitly authorized security decision. Devices and other assigned assets must be returned within {asset_return_business_days} business days after the final date; remote employees use an approved return process. Asset return after departure never extends account access. People Operations closes the checklist after access, handover, assets and final-settlement review are recorded.
